name: useAppFunctions
summary: In-process registry and runner for device actions, plus a probe of the Android AppFunctions service.
plain: Lists the actions this hook can run, runs them, and lets your own code register more handlers. It also reports whether the Android AppFunctions service exists. It does not make your app callable by Gemini.
description: isSupported is an API-level check (36 and above); serviceFound and serviceName come from a lookup of the Android app_function system service. The hook keeps an in-process registry: built-in actions ('check_phone_thermals', 'purge_memory_cache', 'get_device_silicon_info') and custom schemas and handlers added with registerFunction are listed in functions and run by executeFunction, but none of them is registered with the system service, so Gemini and other assistants cannot see them (that needs a native AppFunctionService in your app). An id that is neither custom nor built in is run through the native registry (PixelNative.getAppFunctions: triggerHapticEffect, setTorchLevel, getSiliconStatus, scanNearbyRadios); executeFunction resolves success false with the native message when the effect did not happen (for example an unsupported haptic primitive) and with an unknown-id error for any other id. source is 'hardware' only when the system service was found.

returns.name: isSupported
returns.desc: Whether the device runs Android 16 (API 36) or later. An API-level check, not a service probe.

returns.name: serviceFound
returns.desc: Whether the android.app.appfunctions.IAppFunctionManager system service is active and discoverable on device.

returns.name: apiLevel
returns.desc: Android platform API level reported by the device.

returns.name: serviceName
returns.desc: System service name ('app_function'); null when the service was not found.

returns.name: functions
returns.desc: The hook's built-in schemas plus custom ones registered through this hook. An in-process list, not the system registry.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: Latest execution or system service error.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: Provenance of AppFunctions state. Real hardware with active app_function service reports 'hardware'.

returns.name: executeFunction
returns.desc: Executes a custom handler, a built-in hardware action, or a native registry function. Resolves success false with the reason in error when the function failed or the id is unknown.

returns.name: registerFunction
returns.type: (schema: AppFunctionSchema, handler: (params: Record<string, any>) => Promise<any> | any) => void
returns.desc: Registers a custom AppFunction handler accessible to on-device agents.

actions.name: executeFunction(functionId, params?)
actions.desc: Executes a custom handler, a built-in hardware action, or a native registry function. Resolves success false with the reason in error when the function failed or the id is unknown.

actions.name: registerFunction(schema, handler)
actions.desc: Registers a custom AppFunction handler accessible to on-device agents.
